puzzles.prompt: Guests wipe their boots on me before entering the lodge. What am I?
I am a peaked green tree wearing a white winter coat. What am I?
I am a warm drink of chocolate sipped by the fire. What am I?
I am a wooden runner that carries you downhill over the snow. What am I?
I am punched for a ride up the mountain. What am I?
I am the basket that carries fresh rolls from the kitchen. What am I?
I am the book of blank pages on the desk for guest notes. What am I?
I am the brass piece that opens room seven. What am I?
I am the broom that sweeps snow from the porch. What am I?
I am the chair that creaks and rocks by the window. What am I?
I am the icy lace that forms on the windowpane. What am I?
I am the iron basket that holds the burning logs. What am I?
I am the iron rail where mittens hang to dry. What am I?
I am the jar of peppermints on the front desk. What am I?
I am the jar of sweetness kept beside the tea tins. What am I?
I am the long wooden stick used to poke the logs. What am I?
I am the metal scoop used to clear the front steps. What am I?
I am the packed-snow walk between the lodge and the barn. What am I?
I am the post that points guests up the mountain road. What am I?
I am the smooth surface skaters use on the village pond. What am I?
I am the soft white flake with six arms. What am I?
I am the soft white pile against the lodge door. What am I?
I am the soft wrap wound twice around a guest's neck. What am I?
I am the spare footwear by the mudroom door. What am I?
I am the stack that paints a gray ribbon on the sky. What am I?
I am the stove that warms the kitchen before dawn. What am I?
I am the thick cup that holds the cocoa. What am I?
I am the warm glow left under ash when the fire settles. What am I?
I am the wooden seat that faces the hearth. What am I?
I am the wool cover folded at the foot of every bed. What am I?
I am the wool foot-warmer drying on the hearth rail. What am I?
I am what the stationmaster blows for the Express. What am I?
I am white, soft, and fall from the Frostwood sky. What am I?
I chime the hour in the lodge lobby. What am I?
I crackle and glow in the lodge fireplace. What am I?
I hang above the hearth and ring when someone wants a room. What am I?
I hang on a peg and hold a guest's winter coat. What am I?
I keep cold fingers warm beside the fire. What am I?
I light the path with a warm glow when the lamps flicker. What am I?
I whistle when the water is ready for tea. What am I?

By day I am a still white field; by night skaters carve curves in me. What am I?
The cook says: throw away the outside, cook the inside, then eat the outside and throw away the inside. What was prepared?
Forward I am heavy; backward I am not. Deep snow feels like me. What am I?
Guests climb me to reach the upper rooms, yet I never leave the lobby. What am I?
I am a small room with pegs where guests leave coats and scarves. What am I?
I am a word of five letters. Take away two and one remains—written on the puzzle-night chalkboard. What word am I?
I am always in front of the guest, yet the guest can never see me. What am I?
I am light as a feather, yet no guest can hold me long in mittened hands. What am I?
I am tall when I am young in the candle hall and short when I am old. What am I?
I begin the evening as a log and end it as a quiet glow under ash. What am I?
I can fill every room of the lodge yet take up no space at all. What am I?
I catch smoke for a living and never complain of the heat. What am I?
I go up the mountain with the train and come down with it, yet I never leave my seat. What am I?
I have a face but never frown, hands that never wave, and I keep the lodge on time. What am I?
I have a neck but no head and wear a warm body by the fire. Guests pull me on before a walk. What am I?
I have bark but never bite, needles but never sew, and I wear a white coat all winter. What am I?
I have cities with no houses, forests with no trees, and water with no fish—on the lounge wall. What am I?
I have keys but open no doors; soft tunes follow supper in the lounge. What am I?
I have many teeth but never bite; the cook uses me on carrots for stew. What am I?
I have no wings but I fly up the flue; I have no lungs but I breathe for the fire. What am I?
I run but never walk, have a bed of gravel, and the Express follows me. What am I?
I speak without a mouth across the valley when the whistle blows. What am I?
I stand on one leg with my heart in my head in the kitchen garden pot. What am I?
I travel up the mountain without walking, carry guests without arms, and whistle without lips. What am I?
The lodge letter board has me: I am an English word with three consecutive double letters. What am I?
The more logs you take from the woodpile's center, the bigger I become. What am I?
The more of me there is in the dining hall, the less you see. What am I?
What belongs to the lodgekeeper but is used more by the guests?
What has a head, a tail, is brown, and has no legs—left on the hearth after the fire dies?
